title: Set-valued models of a small finite-limit theory are locally finitely presentable
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $T$ be a $\mathcal U$-small category with all finite limits, and let $\operatorname{Lex}(T,\mathbf{Set}_{\mathcal U})$ be the category of functors preserving finite limits, with natural transformations as morphisms. A limit is a terminal cone and a finite limit is one indexed by a finite category; colimits have the dual universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This category has all $\mathcal U$-small limits and colimits and is locally finitely presentable: there is a $\mathcal U$-small family of objects $P$ such that each $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves filtered colimits and every object is a filtered colimit of members of this family. Limits and filtered colimits of these models are computed pointwise in sets. Here filtered means nonempty, every two objects have a common receiving object, and every parallel pair of arrows is equalized by a further arrow. Equivalently the same conclusions hold for models of any small finite-limit sketch, a small diagram of sorts and operations with specified finite cones required to be limit cones, by passing to its free finite-limit completion.

source.place: G. M. Kelly, Structures defined by finite limits in the enriched context, I (1982), Sections 4 and 9, especially (9.3), (9.4), (9.7), Theorem (9.8), printed pp. 35–36; specialize the base to Set. The sketch formulation uses the free finite-limit completion in (9.3). Read online; not archived. No Stacks tag states this general sketch theorem.
